alalal-e90698-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 12: whether faith comes through sight rather than hearing.

alalal-e90698-d1e113.summary: Introduces the question on Lombard's statement that what is believed before it is understood is not wholly unknown, since faith comes from hearing.

alalal-e90698-d1e127.summary: Argument: faith is a kind of thinking, which arises by discovery or teaching, so it seems to come more through sight than hearing.

alalal-e90698-d1e141.summary: First reason: sight serves discovery and hearing serves teaching, and discovery is superior to teaching.

alalal-e90698-d1e150.summary: Second reason: sight is the nobler sense, informs about more things and gives more certainty about the common sensibles, so faith should come from sight.

alalal-e90698-d1e163.summary: Solution: hearing always receives teaching from another, and since faith comes from a higher light, not from our discovery, hearing suits it more than sight; this answers the first reason.
claims: Faith comes from hearing because it is received from a higher source, not discovered by us.

alalal-e90698-d1e179.summary: Reply to the second: sight is nobler regarding proper objects, but here what is meant is an inner hearing, the reception of knowledge of first truth from another, so the objection is irrelevant.

alalal-e90698.summary: Article 12 asks why faith is said to come from hearing rather than sight, given that sight is the nobler sense and serves discovery, which is superior to teaching. Albert answers that hearing always receives teaching from another. Faith comes from a higher light and not from our own discovery, so it belongs to hearing. The hearing in question is inner: the reception of knowledge of first truth from another.
claims: Faith comes from hearing because it is received from a higher source rather than discovered.
The hearing of faith is an inner reception of first truth from another.
